answer: Weight comes only after one certified restoration of a listed historic building in the heritage registry: a canyon-side chapel surveyed, then signed off by a surveyor, one project per identity. Each fake costs one project: 2,000 units in materials, 350 in fees, 90 days of work, so 100 fakes cost 235,000 units, 100 sites. A crew restoring the sonnet-inscribed doorway cannot bill those days to a second identity. A forged sign-off fails the registry check, a half-finished shell stays dormant, and the grove behind the chapel is inspected too, so scaling fakes means paying full price each time.
